versions.short: The bill would allow federal land agencies to use a share of their existing wildfire and fuels funding for planned, controlled burns known as prescribed fire, including grants and contracts with states, tribes, local governments, and nonprofits to carry them out. It would set up a Collaborative Prescribed Fire Program that funds larger landscape-level burn projects chosen under priority criteria, with spending caps and time limits. It would also require agencies to increase the total acreage burned on federal land each year for ten years, and direct them to build prescribed fire workforce options such as dedicated task forces, training centers, and certification changes. Other parts would extend legal protections to certain non-federal partners working on these burns, direct coordination with air quality agencies on smoke rules, create a national prescribed fire education program, and require annual reports to Congress and to a national fire database.
